course_name_original: Prevención y Control de la Contaminación Atmosférica

learning_outcomes.text: Consult and effectively use atmospheric pollution regulations, identifying legal requirements applicable to industrial facilities and ambient air.
Demonstrate knowledge of equipment used for measuring atmospheric pollutants emitted by industrial facilities (emission) and those existing in ambient air (air quality).

Demonstrate knowledge and understanding of different technologies for the prevention and correction of atmospheric pollution, performing calculations for sizing equipment for the treatment of gaseous effluents.
Prepare and present correctly, both orally and in writing, reports on industrial activities, identifying environmental problems they can generate in ambient air and proposing solutions to them.

syllabus_topics: Regulatory aspects in air quality and atmospheric protection
Effect of thermal inversion and topography on the dispersion of pollutants in the atmosphere. Dispersion of settleable matter
Design and operation of particle purification systems: Cyclones
Design and operation of particle purification systems: Electrofilters
Design and operation of particle purification systems: Bag filters
Design and operation of wet particle purification systems. Venturi scrubbers
Design and operation of gas purification systems: Gas absorption
Design and operation of gas purification systems: Gas adsorption
Design and operation of gas purification systems: Chemical oxidation processes
Specific techniques for the control of gaseous pollutants: nitrogen oxides and sulfur oxides
Carbon dioxide capture and storage technologies
teaching_methods: Classroom practices (exercises, problem solving, group work presentation)
Laboratory practices (sampling and analysis of deposits, measurement of PM10 fraction, absorption of gaseous pollutants, dispersion of pollutants)
assessment_rules: For the ordinary call, if all minimums are met, the final grade is calculated as: [0.6 x (AVERAGE (P1;P2))] + (0.09 x PA) + (0.06 x TG) + (0.15 x PL) + (0.10 x AP). If P1 was not taken or failed, the final grade is calculated as: 0.6 x (E) + (0.09 x PA) + (0.06 x TG) + (0.15 x PL) + (0.10 x AP). A minimum grade of 5 out of 10 is required to pass. In the extraordinary call, the final grade is 0.6 x (E) + (0.09 x PA) + (0.06 x TG) + (0.15 x PL) + (0.10 x AP), with a minimum of 5 to pass. For differentiated evaluation, the final grade is 0.7 x (E) + (0.15 x T) + (0.15 x PL), with a minimum of 5 to pass. Specific minimum scores for each component (e.g., 1.5/5 for theory/problems in exams, 4/10 for PA, TG, PL) and mandatory attendance for group tutorials and lab practices apply. Resit arrangements are detailed for each component failing the minimums.
